headline: 179-unit apartment project at 37 Enon Street: public hearing closed, review continued
summary: The project would include 179 residential units, about 2,600 square feet of retail space, and 22 affordable units at 60% of area median income on a 4.87-acre site where the existing Stop & Shop is located. The applicant's attorney said the project would cut weekday daily vehicle trips by 63% compared with the grocery store, and the applicant agreed to new traffic counts requested by the Parking and Traffic Commission. Separately, the hearing on four single-family houses at 38 Stanley Street was continued. The special permit must be resolved within 90 days of closing the hearing, and site plan review within 65 days.
decisions: Closed the public hearing on the 37 Enon Street housing project.
Continued the 37 Enon Street housing project to December 15th, 7 to nothing.
Continued the 38 Stanley Street open space residential design hearing to December 15th.
discussion: Enon Street traffic counts: Members questioned the July 23 to 25 counts and whether they reflect school-year traffic. The traffic engineer said July counts usually run above average, and the applicant agreed to new counts for the city.
Parking and nearby businesses: Public speakers said there would not be enough parking and that nearby shops would lose spaces. Speakers asked for fewer units or a smaller building.

Building size and lights: An abutter said the building was too large and its lights would reach nearby homes. The applicant's team said its lights would have shields and the plan is designed to keep light within the property.

38 Stanley Street house: Speakers asked the board to save the older house, and one group presented an alternative plan that keeps its core. The applicant's team said restoring the house would cost more than $3 million and that the shoe shed could be moved across the street.
Clean energy review: Members said they want the Clean Energy Advisory Committee's comments before a vote. The applicant asked the board to consider closing the hearing that night.
